01 / THE COURSE PAIR

Learn the mechanism.
Build the system.

Follow the same ideas from a small numerical example to a working application. Every topic has a practical task and something you can verify.

Download the full syllabus ↓
COURSE 0132 HOURS · PROPOSED

Core Principles & Frontier Applications of Large Models

Understand Transformers across language and vision. Study how models learn, generate, and become part of an agent.

ArchitectureLearningLanguage + vision
COURSE 022 WEEKS · PROPOSED

Large Models & AI Agents:
Project Design

Turn the theory into a system that perceives, retrieves, uses tools, and checks its results. Explain both its successes and its failures.

ImplementationIntegrationEvaluation

Planning basis: basic programming and elementary linear algebra, with Python and tensor exercises for preparation. Credits, dates, and final teaching arrangements are to be confirmed.

02 / THE LEARNING PATH

Sixteen lessons.
One connected sequence.

Start with representations. Build the Transformer. Explore language and vision. Give an LLM tools, then test what it can do.

16 lessons · 32 teaching hours
↳

The same block, two applications. Build a miniature language model and a small Vision Transformer before connecting pretrained models to an agent.

03 / THE INTERACTIVE STUDIO

A little less abstract.
A little more hands-on.

Two small examples to explore before opening a notebook. Change an attention pattern, then step through an agent’s actions.

EXPERIMENT 01TRANSFORMERS

Where does attention go?

Select a query and change its visibility. Each row sums to one across the positions it can see.

CHOOSE A QUERY
SharperMore distributed

A toy calculation with fixed Q/K vectors. The patch labels are illustrative; they are not predictions from a trained model.

EXPERIMENT 02LLM AGENTS

Watch a task become actions.

Follow a bounded agent loop from a request to a recommendation supported by tool results.

THE TASK

“Find a model for image classification and suggest a check before I use it.”

Observe→Act→Update→Verify→Stop
↳

The task is ready.
Run the first step to inspect the workflow.

0 / 5

Scripted teaching walkthrough. No live LLM is running here; the full project uses a model to select actions.

04 / THE PROJECT COURSE

Build something.
Prove that it works.

Complete the shared experiments, then work in a team of about three on one integration project. Use a controlled task set to evaluate the result.

TEN DAYS, STEP BY STEP

From a baseline
to a defensible result.

Individual experiments take place during the semester. The project course is for integration, testing, and explanation.

    05 / WHAT COUNTS

    Understand it.
    Explain your choices.

    Assessment rewards working systems and the people who understand them. Each student explains an architecture, traces an agent’s actions, and makes a small live code change.

    AI coding assistance is welcome with disclosure. You remain responsible for the code and the evidence you submit.

    Theory course

    Individual experiments30%
    Quizzes20%
    Final assessment50%

    Project course

    System implementation25%
    Experiments & failure analysis25%
    Engineering & reproducibility15%
    Individual defense & live modification35%

    06 / THE READING SHELF

    Go to the source.

    Selected papers and tutorials, read with a purpose. Start with the diagrams and assigned concepts; full paper derivations are extension material.

    Start with a question.
    Leave with a working model.
